digest.component_or_area: GitHub Actions CI / pytest matrix jobs
propositions: GitHub Actions pytest matrix jobs in gerrit-verify.yaml remain in_progress for 1.7–4.3 hours after reaching 99% progress, then require manual cancellation to unblock the queue, because the test job lacks a timeout-minutes bound and GitHub applies the 360-minute default.

The primary mechanism causing test hangs in stale Gerrit patchsets 1129/1130/1131/1136 is the absence of commit 96a0d5c3f (blob prefetch fix), which leaves materialize_tree performing per-blob lazy-fetch via checkout-index on partial clones, projecting ~2.1 hours for ~25,561 files.

A secondary defect in Gerrit 1129 PS1–PS3 causes test_comment_map_matches_the_shared_contract to timeout because FakeJiraClient.search_issues ignores startAt/maxResults pagination kwargs and returns the same non-empty page forever, causing infinite loop in _paged_search.

Adding timeout-minutes: 60 to jobs.test in _build-and-test.yml bounds the job execution and prevents manual-clear dependence for any recurrence, while preserving the 10–16 minute normal default-suite runtime with >3x macOS margin.

The 60-minute timeout implements the contract documented in _build-and-test.yml and the production-path expectation that hosted runners release after a bounded failure, independently of whether a code defect causes slowness.
